title: The Child Is Revived and Pressed toward Conversion

blocks.text: After extended torment, the child falls into a state that looks like the edge of death, and for a moment Subeg Singh reads the scene as proof that Sikh honor has been preserved. The executioners and court, however, are not prepared to let the drama end there.

Instead, the child is revived and pressed toward conversion, surrounded by those who try to rename his ordeal as rebirth into another faith. This maneuver aims to rewrite the meaning of suffering itself, turning near-death into an instrument of ideological capture.

Subeg Singh is left astonished and heartsore as he watches the regime attempt to manufacture consent out of exhaustion and confusion. The page dwells on that shock in order to show how coercion seeks not only the body but also memory, identity, and speech.
